<|begin_of_text|>If you could put the benefits of exercise in a pill it would easily be the most widely prescribed medication in the world.
The effects of exercise are well known in terms of stabilizing blood sugar levels - ideal for any kid taking heavy doses of insulin. It helps the body run more efficiently - allowing better delivery to where you need your insulin to be absorbed - be it fat, muscles or some tissues such as the kidney that have stopped absorbing. It also contributes to stress reduction (by producing those dopamines) which helps stop those kids that have so much anxiety that they will not do activities because they have low self confidence. It all seems very basic. So how come this appears to be such a complex issue?
The fact that we are not a physically active society is the start of the problem.
